column1:
Hawkish policy stance with mixed credit conditions. The March 16, 2022 FOMC statement marks a 25 bp liftoff, guidance for ongoing increases, and soon-to-begin balance sheet reduction amid elevated, broad-based inflation and Ukraine-related upside inflation risk and downside growth risk.

SLOOS lens:
- Banks had eased standards for C&I and CRE and reported stronger demand from large, middle-market, and small firms; banks expected improvement in business/CRE and non-syndicated C&I loan performance, suggesting supportive credit supply for investment and hiring.
- Banks expected interest rates to rise, reported weaker demand for residential real estate (including GSE and subprime) and expected deterioration in household credit segments (auto, credit cards, nonconforming jumbo), pointing to cooling consumer credit and housing.
- Net, SLOOS implies business credit is a partial cushion to growth, but consumer-side and housing headwinds still lean the outlook negative as policy tightens.

Adjusted tone: cautious and growth-negative, but slightly less negative than an FSR-only read because business credit supply remains supportive.
